verdicts.conditionQuote: with a short-lived signed URL, so large files never pass through our own services
verdicts.claimQuote: Clients upload a photo directly to object storage
verdicts.note: Mechanism and rationale for the direct upload, not a limit on another claim.

verdicts.conditionQuote: applies a rate limit of 120 requests per minute per account
verdicts.claimQuote: routes the request to the right service
verdicts.note: A real numeric limit on gateway traffic; the routing claim stays broadly true.

verdicts.conditionQuote: If the auth service cannot be reached, the gateway rejects the request instead of letting it through unchecked.
verdicts.claimQuote: checks the caller's access token with the auth service
verdicts.note: Fail-closed behaviour of the token check; important but the check claim stays true without it.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Photo bytes are served to clients by the CDN, never by the gateway.
verdicts.claimQuote: Every client request enters through the API gateway.
verdicts.note: Photo byte fetches (and direct uploads) bypass the gateway, so 'every client request' is misleading without this exception.

verdicts.conditionQuote: followers who have notifications turned on
verdicts.claimQuote: asks the push-notification provider to alert followers
verdicts.note: Dropping the scope makes the alert claim (and the u32 flow step) read as alerting all followers.

verdicts.conditionQuote: The queue keeps an event for up to 7 days
verdicts.claimQuote: a worker outage delays thumbnails but does not lose uploads
verdicts.note: 'Does not lose uploads' is false for an outage longer than 7 days.

verdicts.conditionQuote: A photo whose processing keeps failing stays in the "processing" state and is not shown in any feed.
verdicts.claimQuote: the feed service adds the photo to the followers' feeds
verdicts.note: Failure-path outcome of the posting flow; the success-path description stays true.

verdicts.claimQuote: keeps ready-made feed pages in the cache
verdicts.note: Cache lifetime bound (staleness window); claim stays true.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Pinhole only sends it requests and does not control when an alert arrives
verdicts.claimQuote: asks the push-notification provider to alert followers who have notifications turned on
verdicts.note: Delivery-timing caveat on the alerting step.

verdicts.conditionQuote: The cost is that a new photo takes a few seconds to appear in feeds.
verdicts.claimQuote: the upload service and the workers only meet through the message queue
verdicts.note: Stated trade-off of the queue decision.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Originals can be up to 25 MB
verdicts.claimQuote: clients send bytes straight to object storage and the upload service only signs the URL and records the result
verdicts.note: Mainly rationale, but it also states the size bound on originals, which a reader should keep.

verdicts.conditionQuote: we accept that their outages are outside our control
verdicts.claimQuote: We use a third-party CDN and push-notification provider instead of running our own
verdicts.note: Accepted risk of the buy decision.

verdicts.conditionQuote: How failed processing is retried, and when a stuck photo is cleaned up, is not decided yet.
verdicts.claimQuote: A photo whose processing keeps failing stays in the "processing" state and is not shown in any feed.
verdicts.note: Open question on the failure path; the stated behaviour holds for now.

additional.conditionQuote: The design is sized for about 2 million daily active users at launch.
additional.claimQuote: Pinhole lets people post photos and see the photos of the accounts they follow in a feed.
additional.note: Capacity scope of the whole design; no single claim sentence it limits, so linked to the system statement.

additional.conditionQuote: Whether the feed service should precompute feeds for accounts with very many followers is left to the feed service's own low-level design.
additional.claimQuote: The feed service builds each person's feed from the photos of the accounts they follow
additional.note: Open question on how feed building scales for high-follower accounts.
